s: Alexander's empire is divided. Antiochus Epiphanes plunders the temple, sets up an abomination on the altar and forces pagan ways on Israel.
Mattathias refuses to sacrifice to idols and flees to the hills with his sons to defend the law.
Judas Maccabeus takes his father's place and wins victories against the Syrian generals.
Judas defeats Gorgias and Lysias, then cleanses and rededicates the temple, the feast later called Hanukkah.
Judas and his brothers rescue Jews in Galilee and Gilead.
Antiochus dies in grief. The Syrians return with elephants and Eleazar dies bravely.
Demetrius sends Bacchides and Nicanor against Judas. Nicanor is defeated and killed.
Judas makes a treaty of friendship with Rome.
Judas falls in battle and Jonathan becomes leader.
Rival kings court Jonathan, and he becomes high priest.
Ptolemy of Egypt intervenes. Jonathan wins favour with Demetrius.
Jonathan renews ties with Rome and Sparta and is captured by treachery.
Simon takes command after Jonathan is killed, and Judea becomes independent.
Simon's peaceful rule is praised, and he is honoured as leader and high priest.
Antiochus VII makes promises to Simon, then turns against him.
Simon is murdered by his son-in-law, and his son John becomes leader.

1: A pagan king sets up an idol on the temple altar and forbids the Jewish faith. Faithful Jews must choose between God's law and their lives.
4: Judas Maccabeus cleanses the temple and restores worship. The Jewish feast of Hanukkah remembers this day.
